name: BD-JB - Blu-ray Disc Java Xlet to native code (TheFloW)
subsystem: userland/bd-j (kernel access needs a separate kernel exploit)

root_cause.summary: The BD-J Xlet runs in a JVM whose boot classpath includes bdjstack.jar, so several bdjstack classes execute with full permissions on attacker-influenced input. UserPreferenceManagerImpl deserializes the user-writable userprefs file inside AccessController.doPrivileged; IxcProxy.invokeMethod reflectively invokes public methods in a privileged context; and on PS4 com.oracle.security.Service.newInstance resolves arbitrary class names. The chain disables the SecurityManager, reaches native memory and symbols through sun.misc.Unsafe and ClassLoader$NativeLibrary.findEntry, and on PS4 sends a 0x58-byte CompilerAgentRequest to the separate JIT compiler process, whose compiler_data pointer at offset 0x38 is used as the destination of a memcpy into shared JIT memory. The result is native userland code execution; this is not itself a kernel bug.
root_cause.primitive: Java sandbox escape to AllPermission plus arbitrary native calls; on PS4 a write-what-where into a shared JIT page through the compiler agent
root_cause.trigger: insert a burned Blu-ray whose BD-J Xlet contains the chain and open the Blu-ray player
root_cause.consequence: arbitrary native code execution in the BD-J process (userland); kernel compromise requires chaining a separate kernel exploit

discovery_approach.summary: TheFloW treated the Blu-ray player as an alternative entry point because PS5 WebKit was constrained by XOM and a stricter sandbox. He searched bdjstack.jar for AccessController.doPrivileged call sites, found the privileged deserialization and IxcProxy invocation gadgets, added the PS4-only com.oracle.security.Service constructor gadget, and used the CompilerAgentRequest write for JIT code execution. The five issues were reported to PlayStation on 2021-10-25 (HackerOne #1379975), presented at hardwear.io on 2022-06-10 and disclosed the same day.
signals: ObjectInputStream.readObject() on RootCertManager.getOriginalPersistentRoot() + "/userprefs" inside a doPrivileged action
CompilerAgentRequest is 0x58 bytes and its compiler_data field at +0x38 is passed to memcpy(req.compiler_data + 0x28, &req, 0x58)
PS4-only class com.oracle.security.Service.newInstance calling Class.forName on a caller-supplied name

firmware.fixed_in: 9.50 (PS4) / 5.00 (PS5) per the author's June 2022 support statement; no per-gadget patch map is public
differences: PS4 runs the JVM JIT in a separate compiler process and the runtime writes payloads into shared JIT pages through CompilerAgentRequest; PS5 has no JVM JIT, so the compiler-agent stage does not exist there (slides).
com.oracle.security.Service is a PS4-only gadget; the PS5 BD-JB implementations instead used sleirsgoevy's jdk.internal-based sandbox escape (PS5 wiki).

The same HackerOne report includes a UDF kernel overflow (udf_read_internal copying inf_len bytes into a sector_size buffer), but the public payload only panics the kernel; it is a separate kernel bug from the BD-J sandbox escape.

patch_evidence.what: no public patch diff for the individual BD-J gadgets; the slides give only a support ceiling (PS4 <9.50, PS5 <5.00), and the HackerOne report says only that it was tested on 9.00
patch_evidence.limits: no firmware bytes, no Sony advisory text and no binary diff are stored or linked here

sources.supports: the five chained BD-J vulnerabilities (userprefs readObject, IxcProxy, com.oracle.security.Service, CompilerAgentRequest memcpy at +0x38, UDF inf_len/sector_size overflow), tested on 9.00, disclosed 2022-06-10

JVM boot classpath includes bdjstack.jar; userprefs path /OS/HDD/download0/mnt_ada/userprefs; IxcProxy privileged invocation; PS4 compiler process versus no JVM JIT on PS5; support PS4 <9.50 and PS5 <5.00
BD-JB five-vulnerability chain at <=9.00, the PS4/PS5 bdjstack paths, and the later BD-JB2/BD-JB-EX variants used for the firmware-difference claims
PS5 BD-JB at <=4.51, the PS5 alternative jdk.internal sandbox escape, and the fact that the PS4-only Service gadget did not work on PS5
public 'first bd-j hack' implementation repository, created 2021-10-22
the end-to-end disc workflow and the later Lapse.iso (9.00-12.02) and Henloader (9.00-12.52) chains that pair BD-JB with a kernel exploit

gaps: No public patch diff for the individual BD-J gadgets; the <9.50/<5.00 ceiling is the author's support statement, not a vendor advisory.
The UDF overflow in the same report is demonstrated only as a kernel panic; no fetched source shows it reaching controlled kernel code execution.
The PS5 implementations (sleirsgoevy, john-tornblom, psxdev) replace the PS4-only stages, but the fetched sources do not give a single canonical PS5 chain.
The HackerOne report does not map each vulnerability to a firmware version; 'tested on latest 9.00' is the only concrete test statement.

entry_chain.stage: Burned Blu-ray inserted; the Blu-ray player mounts the UDF volume and starts the BD-J Xlet from BDMV/BDJO
entry_chain.image_visible: BDMV/BDJO descriptors and the JAR entries are on the disc; the kernel image alone does not contain the BD-J Java classes. The system_ex BD-J launcher contains the -Xbootclasspath string and bdjstack.jar.
entry_chain.runtime_only: which Xlet entry point the player invokes and the exact JVM launch state

entry_chain.stage: Attacker Java runs inside the BD-J security sandbox
entry_chain.image_visible: JAR manifest/Main-Class and bytecode references to bdjstack classes; the kernel image shows none of this
entry_chain.runtime_only: the protection domains and permissions actually assigned to the Xlet

entry_chain.stage: Sandbox escape through bdjstack privileged-context gadgets (userprefs deserialization, IxcProxy, PS4 Service gadget)
entry_chain.image_visible: strings and bytecode references to AccessController.doPrivileged, ObjectInputStream, IxcProxy and Service.newInstance in bdjstack.jar; nothing in the kernel image
entry_chain.runtime_only: the serialized object graph, the reachable constructors and the resulting AllPermission grant

entry_chain.stage: SecurityManager disabled; sun.misc.Unsafe and NativeLibrary.findEntry give native memory access and symbol lookup
entry_chain.image_visible: Unsafe and NativeLibrary symbols in rt.jar/bdjstack.jar; no kernel-image signature
entry_chain.runtime_only: the resolved libkernel addresses, fake ArrayKlass layout and the setjmp/__Ux86_64_setcontext call

entry_chain.stage: PS4: CompilerAgentRequest write into a shared JIT page; PS5: native calls without JVM JIT
entry_chain.image_visible: CompilerAgentRequest structure and its memcpy are in the BD-J runtime; PS5's lack of the compiler process is a platform property
entry_chain.runtime_only: the JIT page address, the compiler socket and the payload placement

entry_chain.stage: Separate kernel exploit selected for the firmware (for example Lapse aio_multi_delete on PS4 9.00-12.02, or an IPv6/umtx/netcontrol bug on PS5)
entry_chain.image_visible: the kernel image contains the candidate bug sites (aio_multi_delete, ip6_setpktopt, umtx_shm_unref_reg_locked, netcontrol); UDF udf_read_internal is visible if that path is used
entry_chain.runtime_only: which bug matches the running firmware, the heap layout and the KASLR/offset state
